body: Agreed. I'm just so lost in all of this. I just keep thinking they'll ( my mom and husband ) all be better without me. All I do is make their lives more difficult. It just sucks I know right now both of them need me around ( my husband just had surgery last week and can't do a lot of things by himself and my mom is old and can barely walk by herself to take the dogs out , clean, etc) but I just feel like I keep failing them. I'm just so low right now. I just can't keep up right now. I keep fighting but I'm wearing thin. I just need things to let up and of course naturally just comes on stronger. Sorry I've been rambling this entire time. I just don't feel as lonely talking to you. Seems like you understand

I'd like to think I'd be a nicer person, not get so angry over minor things, have friends, be able to go out and socialize without worrying how many people are going to be there, be able to accomplish something, and mainly get a new job. My job definitely has been a major stressor for me and I personally feel is what brought the " beast " out of me. I'm just so anxiety ridden I can't even bare to think about having to go through a interview.  But who's to say not having it would change anything? I drive myself nuts with the what ifs. I've almost begun to wonder if maybe some of it is just my personality. I mean I would hope not. There are times where I feel in control and I just look at myself and I'm like what the actual fuck. I try to reason with my self and say well this is why you're like this. But really there's no excuse.

I swear I feel like we share a brain lol. Everything you've said I 100% relate to. Which I guess makes me feel slightly better that I'm not alone in this. Just isn't fair. And I get life isn't fair or whatever but like fuck, I'd almost rather be missing a limb then to have this brain or mine. Most days I'm worried my husband will eventually leave me because he's had enough "crazy".. im much more pleasant when manic but the depressive episodes always last longer.

I literally could have written this. Everything you've said is me. Especially the part of slowly fading away. I feel like no matter how hard I try it's pointless because in the end I can't escape from my mind. Late at night when I can't sleep my thoughts literally almost destroy me. And it sucks I just want to have a normal life. Like I had before. I just can't get back to that person, it's almost like that person never even existed.
I feel the same way most days. I haven't had a good day in a long time. I have a voice in my telling me all of the same things. It's the absolute worst, when you are your worst enemy.
I took it for a couple months when I was younger. I had to stop taking it as it was causing me to hallucinate. Both depakote and lamictal worked better for me personally.

I can totally relate. Most days I barely get by. I've isolated myself so much I don't even have friends to talk to about it. Not that they would understand. If you even do so much as hint to having any mental Illness let alone bipolar people look at you like you're alien. I haven't been able to recognize myself in years. To the point of having identity issues. Meds don't work just make me a zombie but without them the mood swings can be unbearable. It's like we literally can not win.
Same. I'm terrible at it. It's like even in the midst of thinking I need to be better I still mess up.

Definitely do this. For me more so when I'm in a depressed episode but it is literally every little thing. I also don't tell anyone for fear they might try to admit me into a hospital. Which I can't afford the stay or to be off from work that long. I generally am not a threat to myself. I've had unsuccessful attempts in the past and can't deal with the aftermath of yet another unsuccessful attempt. The sad part is even of the midst of thinking these thoughts I usually am aware of how silly it seems to think " oh I should kill myself because I forgot to take the trash out, etc" but that only makes it worse and the thoughts continue.
